q: The circuit complexity of a Boolean function f: {0,1}ⁿ → {0,1} is the size of the smallest Boolean circuit computing f. Shannon's counting argument shows:
opts: Most Boolean functions require exponential circuit size (Ω(2ⁿ/n))
No function requires more than n² gates
exp: Shannon's counting argument (1949): there are 2^{2ⁿ} functions but only ≈ (nS)^S circuits of size S. For S = c·2ⁿ/n with small c, most functions cannot be computed. This shows explicit hard functions exist but doesn't exhibit them.
